```{r, include = FALSE}
# all examples are run (and shown as interactive players), except when building the package for CRAN, where
# only the lighter examples are run so the package stays small (< 5 MB) and no files are downloaded. To build
# for CRAN set the environment variable DYNASPEC_CRAN before building, e.g.:
#   Sys.setenv(DYNASPEC_CRAN = "true"); devtools::build()
full <- !identical(Sys.getenv("DYNASPEC_CRAN"), "true")

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  message = FALSE,
  eval = full
)
```

dynaSpec creates dynamic spectrograms: spectrograms that move along with the sound. They are built in layers, as 'ggplot2' graphs: `dynaspec()` takes the sound, and layers are added with `+`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
dynaspec(wave, flim = c(1, 10)) +      # the sound (and frequency and time ranges)
  spectrogram(wl = 300, pal = viridis) + # how the spectrogram is computed and drawn
  oscillogram() +                        # add an oscillogram
  selections(st) +                       # highlight parts of the sound
  annotations("song", start = 0, end = 2) + # label parts of the sound
  player(speeds = c(1, 0.5)) +           # playback buttons
  scrolling(t.display = 1.7)             # style: scrolling(), paged() or static()
```

There are three styles of dynamic spectrograms:

- [Static spectrograms](#static-spectrograms) (`static()`, the default): a play line moves over the whole spectrogram (and oscillogram)
- [Scrolling spectrograms](#scrolling-spectrograms) (`scrolling()`): the spectrogram scrolls along a fixed play line
- [Paged spectrograms](#paged-spectrograms) (`paged()`): pages of the spectrogram are revealed as the sound plays

Printing a `dynaspec` object shows an interactive web page: press play to watch the spectrogram along with the sound, click on it to play from that point, and use the speed buttons to slow the sound down. In the R console web pages are shown in the RStudio viewer (or the web browser), and in R Markdown and Quarto documents (like this vignette) they are embedded in the document. Figures and sounds are embedded in the HTML code, so the pages can also be saved with `save_dynaspec()` and shared as single files or pasted into any web page. `save_dynaspec()` also creates videos (`.mp4`), which can be used where web pages cannot, such as presentation slides or social media (see [Saving web pages, videos and images](#saving-web-pages-videos-and-images)).

```{r, eval = TRUE}
library(dynaSpec)
library(viridis)
library(seewave)
```

Some examples use recordings from the package [NatureSounds](https://cran.r-project.org/package=NatureSounds) or downloaded from the web.

## Static spectrograms

Static spectrograms show the whole sound at once: a line moves over the spectrogram and oscillogram as the sound plays. This is the default style:

```{r, eval = TRUE}
data("canyon_wren")

dynaspec(canyon_wren, flim = c(1, 10)) +
  spectrogram(wl = 300) +
  oscillogram()
```

As in the other styles, the speed buttons slow the sound down. Slowing down also lowers the pitch (as when slowing down a tape), which makes fast features such as pulses easier to hear. The *keep pitch* button switches to slowing down while keeping the original pitch.

Layers can be stored in an object and modified by adding more layers. Arguments of spectrogram and style layers are combined with the previous ones, while oscillogram and player layers replace the previous ones. For instance, the oscillogram can go above the spectrogram, and colors can be customized. The color of the play line and active buttons is set with `lcol`:

```{r}
cols <- mako(10)

wren <- dynaspec(canyon_wren, flim = c(1, 10)) +
  spectrogram(wl = 300, pal = mako, collevels = seq(-140, 0, 1))

wren +
  oscillogram(position = "above", col = cols[3]) +
  static(lcol = cols[9])
```

Without `oscillogram()` only the spectrogram is shown, and `static(spectro = FALSE)` shows only the oscillogram. Long sounds can be split in several rows with `rows` (`height` sets the height of each row):

```{r}
wren + static(rows = 2, height = 350)
```

Several players can be included in the same document or web page; only one sound plays at a time.

### Sound buttons

`sound_buttons()` creates a row of buttons, each one playing a sound, along with the speed buttons. This is useful to compare sounds:

```{r, eval = TRUE}
first_song <- cutw(canyon_wren, from = 0, to = 1.4, output = "Wave")
last_song <- cutw(canyon_wren, from = 3.8, to = 5.2, output = "Wave")

sound_buttons(list("Start of the song" = first_song, "End of the song" = last_song))
```

## Scrolling spectrograms

*Marcelo's approach.* The spectrogram scrolls along a fixed play line, as in the Macaulay Library. `t.display` sets the time window (in s) shown at once. A scrolling spectrogram of the canyon wren song with a viridis color palette:

```{r, eval = TRUE}
wren <- dynaspec(canyon_wren, flim = c(1, 9)) +
  spectrogram(wl = 300, pal = viridis) +
  scrolling(t.display = 1.7, width = 1000, height = 500, res = 120)

wren
```

By default the lower panel shows the whole sound, with the part being shown highlighted (use `scrolling(overview = FALSE)` to remove it). Black and white spectrogram:

```{r}
wren + spectrogram(pal = reverse.gray.colors.1, collevels = seq(-100, 0, 5))
```

A spectrogram with black background (`colbg = "black"`):

```{r}
wren + spectrogram(colbg = "black")
```

Start playing at 1/2 speed (`speed = 0.5`, which can be changed with the speed buttons) with an oscillogram at the bottom:

```{r}
wren +
  spectrogram(colbg = "black") +
  oscillogram(col = "#31688E99") +
  scrolling(speed = 0.5)
```

Long-billed hermit song at 1/5 speed (`speed = 0.2`), removing axes and looping (`loop = 3`; web pages loop until paused):

```{r}
data("Phae.long4", package = "NatureSounds")

dynaspec(Phae.long4, flim = c(1, 10)) +
  spectrogram(wl = 300, ovlp = 90, pal = magma, collevels = seq(-50, 0, 5), colbg = "black") +
  scrolling(t.display = 1.7, width = 1000, height = 500, res = 120, speed = 0.2, axis.type = "none", loop = 3)
```

The first 20 s of a northern nightingale wren recording from [xeno-canto](https://www.xeno-canto.org) using a custom color palette. Sounds must be in R (as 'Wave' objects) or in local files ('.wav' or '.mp3'), so the recording is downloaded first:

```{r}
nightingale_wren <- tempfile(fileext = ".mp3")
download.file("https://xeno-canto.org/518334/download", nightingale_wren, mode = "wb")

custom_pal <- colorRampPalette(c("#2d2d86", "#2d2d86", reverse.terrain.colors(10)[5:10]))

dynaspec(nightingale_wren, flim = c(2, 8), crop = 20) +
  spectrogram(wl = 600, ovlp = 95, pal = custom_pal, collevels = seq(-40, 0, 5), colbg = "#2d2d86") +
  scrolling(t.display = 3, width = 700, height = 250, res = 100, lcol = "#FFFFFFE6")
```

Spix's disc-winged bat inquiry call slowed down 16 times (`speed = 0.0625`, the slowest speed web browsers can play):

```{r}
data("thyroptera.est", package = "NatureSounds")

# extract one call
thy_wav <- attributes(thyroptera.est)$wave.objects[[12]]

# convert to 16 bits (as the silence added below)
thy_wav <- tuneR::normalize(thy_wav, unit = "16")

# add silence at both sides
thy_wav <- pastew(tuneR::silence(duration = 0.05, samp.rate = thy_wav@samp.rate, xunit = "time"),
                  thy_wav, output = "Wave")
thy_wav <- pastew(thy_wav, tuneR::silence(duration = 0.04, samp.rate = thy_wav@samp.rate, xunit = "time"),
                  output = "Wave")

dynaspec(thy_wav, flim = c(12, 37)) +
  spectrogram(wl = 400, ovlp = 95, pal = inferno, collevels = seq(-40, 0, 5), colbg = "black") +
  oscillogram(col = inferno(10, alpha = 0.9)[3]) +
  scrolling(t.display = 0.08, width = 700, height = 250, res = 100, lcol = "#FFFFFFE6", lty = 1,
            speed = 0.0625, buffer = 0, loop = 4)
```

Selections and labels can also be added to scrolling spectrograms (see [Highlighting and labeling sounds](#highlighting-and-labeling-sounds)). The article [Customizing scrolling spectrograms](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/articles/customizing_scrolling_spectrograms.html) on the package website has more examples.

## Paged spectrograms

*Matt's approach.* The spectrogram is split into "pages", and a translucent box reveals the part of each page being played, as in Adobe Audition's spectral view. Pages turn as the sound plays.

Two example recordings of barn swallows are included in the package:

```{r, eval = TRUE}
# example WAV files included with dynaSpec
f <- list.files(system.file(package = "dynaSpec"), pattern = "\\.wav$", full.names = TRUE)

dynaspec(f[1]) + paged()
```

Settings not supplied take the defaults of each style. For instance, paged spectrograms use the 'inferno' palette and no axes by default. Let's add axes:

```{r, eval = TRUE}
swallow <- dynaspec(f[1]) + paged(axis.type = "standard")

swallow
```

### Brighten the spectrogram

* `amp.trans = 3` is a nonlinear signal booster. It collapses the difference between the loudest and quietest values (higher values = brighter spectrograms); 1 (default) means no transformation
* `collevels = seq(-35, 0, 1)` lowers the amplitude threshold to include some quieter sounds (the default lower limit is -30 dB)
* `bg.flood = TRUE` makes the axis area the same color as the plot background. Axis font switches automatically to white if the background is too dark

```{r}
swallow +
  spectrogram(amp.trans = 3, collevels = seq(-35, 0, 1)) +
  paged(bg.flood = TRUE)
```

### Multi-page spectrograms from longer recordings

In this example:

* `crop = 12` only uses the first 12 seconds of the file (an interval can be given as `crop = c(start, end)`)
* `t.display = 3` sets the "page window", i.e. how many seconds each page displays
* `flim = c(0, 0.7)` limits the frequency axis to the range used by humpback whales (0-700 Hz)
* axes and labels are not plotted by default (`axis.type = "none"`)

```{r}
whale <- tempfile(fileext = ".wav")
download.file("http://www.oceanmammalinst.org/songs/hmpback3.wav", whale, mode = "wb")

dynaspec(whale, flim = c(0, 0.7), crop = 12) +
  spectrogram(amp.trans = 3) +
  paged(t.display = 3)
#Voila 🐋
```

### A common nighthawk call from Xeno-Canto with a custom color scheme

MP3 files are converted automatically. Custom palettes for paged spectrograms can be defined by two colors (start and end of the gradient), the name of a 'viridis' palette (e.g. "magma") or a palette function:

```{r}
nighthawk <- tempfile(fileext = ".mp3")
download.file("https://xeno-canto.org/490771/download", nighthawk, mode = "wb")

dynaspec(nighthawk, crop = 20) +
  spectrogram(pal = c("white", "black")) +
  paged(t.display = 4, highlight.col = "#d1b0ff", lcol = "#7817ff")
```

## Highlighting and labeling sounds

`selections()` highlights parts of the sound with translucent boxes, taking a data frame with the start and end of each selection (in s), as the selection tables of [warbleR](https://cran.r-project.org/package=warbleR) and [ohun](https://cran.r-project.org/package=ohun). If the data frame has 'bottom.freq' and 'top.freq' columns (in kHz) the boxes only span that frequency range. Colors and labels can be taken from columns of the data frame. `annotations()` adds labels shown during a time range of the sound. Both work in the three styles:

```{r, eval = TRUE}
st <- data.frame(
  start = c(0.4, 3.6),
  end = c(1.5, 4.8),
  bottom.freq = c(2, 1.5),
  top.freq = c(9, 5),
  labels = c("first notes", "last notes"),
  colors = c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9")
)

wren <- dynaspec(canyon_wren, flim = c(1, 10)) +
  spectrogram(wl = 300) +
  selections(st, col = "colors", labels = "labels")

wren
```

In scrolling spectrograms the labels of `annotations()` stay at a fixed position, and fade in and out (`fading`, in s) while their time range reaches the play line:

```{r}
wren +
  annotations("canyon wren", start = 0, end = 5.3, x = 0.2, y = 0.9, font = 3, fading = 0.3) +
  scrolling(t.display = 1.7)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Saving web pages, videos and images

`save_dynaspec()` saves `dynaspec` objects. The extension of the file sets the output:

* `.html`: interactive web page
* `.mp4`: video, with the same settings. Videos can be used where web pages cannot, such as presentation slides (e.g. PowerPoint) or social media. [ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html) must be installed to create videos (see the installation instructions in the [README](https://github.com/maRce10/dynaSpec#installation))
* `.png`: still image of static spectrograms, or one image per page of paged spectrograms

```{r, eval = FALSE}
wren <- dynaspec(canyon_wren, flim = c(1, 10)) + spectrogram(wl = 300) + oscillogram()

save_dynaspec(wren, "canyon_wren.html")
save_dynaspec(wren, "canyon_wren.png")
save_dynaspec(wren, "canyon_wren_static.mp4")
save_dynaspec(wren + scrolling(t.display = 1.7), "canyon_wren_scrolling.mp4")
save_dynaspec(swallow, "femaleBarnSwallow.mp4")
```

Videos of static and paged spectrograms are created in a few seconds. Videos of scrolling spectrograms are time consuming, as every frame is rendered. This can be sped up by using several cores (e.g. `scrolling(parallel = 4)`) and by lowering the number of frames per second (`scrolling(fps = 25)`).

Note that embedding sounds makes web pages larger (about 1.4 times the size of the sound file), so cut (e.g. with `crop`) or downsample long recordings before creating web pages.
